thread.title: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney
thread.title_full: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney

author: empire state today
title: Livingston County appoints Matthew Lenahan as new county attorney
text:
Matthew Lenahan has been appointed as the new county attorney for Livingston County, according to a May 13 announcement from the board of supervisors. Lenahan will begin his duties on June 29.
The appointment is significant for Livingston County, as the county attorney serves as the primary legal advisor to the board of supervisors and guides officials through legal matters that affect residents and communities. The position also involves representing the county in civil actions and proceedings involving local government entities.
Lenahan brings more than two decades of legal experience to his new role. He was previously a partner at Rupp Pfalzgraf LLC, handling litigation in state and federal courts, and has served since 2019 as village attorney for both Lima and Honeoye Falls. He said his work with municipal entities has given him an understanding of local government operations: “Matt’s experience with municipal law and his track record of providing sound counsel to local villages made him the ideal choice for this role,” said Board Chair David LeFeber. “We look forward to working alongside him to navigate the legal landscape of local government.”
County Administrator Shannon Hillier, who held the position from 2017 until her promotion in 2025, also commented on Lenahan’s appointment: “Matt brings exceptional legal experience, sound judgment, and professional expertise to this key County position,” said Hillier. “The board and I are confident his leadership will strengthen our operations and support the board and County staff in advancing our goals. We look forward to the positive impact Matt will make in this important role.”
Lenahan expressed enthusiasm about joining Livingston County government: “I was drawn to the opportunity to serve in a public role at the county level and to work on issues that directly affect the residents and communities of Livingston County,” he said. He added that he sees himself not only as a legal advisor but also as a public servant: “The job is not just about addressing legal issues when they arise, but also helping the County make thoughtful, well-informed decisions that serve the public interest and further the interests of the County.”
Lenahan holds degrees from SUNY College at Fredonia (bachelor’s) and University of Pittsburgh School of Law (juris doctor). He is active in community organizations including serving as president of Landmark Society of Western New York’s board.
